CHAPTER ONE

The lamp room smelled of brass polish and old smoke. Mara climbed the last
of the spiral stairs with the evening's oil can knocking against her knee.

"The wick wants trimming again," said Mara.

Tom said, "Then trim it, and stop announcing the weather."

Mara set down the oil can. "One day this tower will fall into the sea."

Beside Tom, the logbook lay open to a blank page. "Not while I keep the
light," he said.

* * *

Wind came up hard after dark. The two of them stood at the gallery rail,
watching the whitecaps chew at the rocks below.

"There's a boat out past the shoals," Mara said, "and no running lights."

"Fishermen, maybe."

"Not in this weather."

"Then signal the harbor."

Somewhere below, a door banged against its frame.

"Whoever built this place loved the sound of slamming doors."

CHAPTER TWO

Morning found the beach strewn with kelp and splintered planking, the sea
flat and unrepentant.

"Nothing with a name on it," he muttered.
